newsitem.title: USA: Orange County agency suspends portfolio manager.
newsitem.headline: Orange County agency suspends portfolio manager.

text.p: The Orange County, Calif., Transportation Authority suspended one of its portfolio managers for allegedly violating its new investment policies, authority officials said on Thursday.
The authority's board of directors suspended BlackRock Financial Management for 12 months, Jim Kenan, the authority's director of finance and administration, said.
The firm was one of four private-sector investment managers under contract with the authority.
The firm was not immediately available to comment on the decision.

BlackRock managed a large portion of the authority's investment portfolio. As of late January, the firm was responsible for investing about $130 million of the authority's $730 million portfolio, Kenan said. The firm was one of the agency's top performing managers, he added.
The firm was suspended because it violated certain of the authority's investment policies, which limit the size and type of securities the authority can purchase.
The policies were adopted in February 1995 in response to the Orange County investment crisis and bankruptcy.
"We have a strict policy and they (BlackRock) were out of compliance with that policy," Kenan said.
Kenan described BlackRock's violations as "technical" in nature. "At no point in time was the authority ever at any financial risk," he said.
In 12 months, BlackRock can reapply to become an active manager for the authority.
Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on Dec. 6, 1994 after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion.
The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.

The Orange County Transportation Authority, which provides bus and other transportation services and funds local freeway construction, suffered heavy losses when the county's investments crashed in 1994.
